identity_scope: Existing peter_brown profile reused for Peter Robert Lamont Brown, born Dublin 1935, Princeton historian of late antiquity. Specific institutional bibliography and primary interviews establish identity; distinct from Peter Hume Brown and other Peter Brown authors. Earlier revival roster and cultural_form strand, including Stone’s portrait-versus-narrative distinction, are preserved. No QID or raw author-key merge.

relations.relationship: Brown credits anthropology’s study of particular societies with helping place religious beliefs within ordinary social life.
relations.evidence_note: Incoming resource acknowledgment, own final 2024 answer. This names a disciplinary resource through Brown’s testimony; it is not a collective anthropologists’ endorsement, universal causal claim or invented mentorship.

relations.relationship: Defends the historical past’s integrity and difference from present concerns against misleading contemporary analogies.
relations.evidence_note: Own 2024 answers on the historian’s task, the Roman-decline analogy and historical truth. His normative position remains attributed, without claiming an exhaustive theory of objectivity.

relations.relationship: Reconstructs Augustine through friendship and communal experiments rather than isolating a celebrated religious figure.
relations.evidence_note: Complete primary 2026 interview, opening and questions on changing friendships and monastic life. Biographical contribution is grounded in his specific argument; reported manuscript discoveries and translations were not independently checked.
